 --> Andhra Pradesh school holidays: These districts to remain closed due to Cyclone Arnab; check details here
 Andhra Pradesh announces school holidays in four districts on October 27 amid Cyclone Arnab warnings, with closures extending to October 29 in Anakapalli. 
 Sheetal Kumari 
 October 26, 2026 / 18:29 IST Share --> 
 -->

 Visakhapatnam and other areas declare holidays.
 IMD warns of heavy rain and strong winds.

 Schools and colleges in several districts of Andhra Pradesh will remain closed on October 27, 2026, as authorities take precautionary measures against Cyclone Arnab, which is approaching the state’s coastline. District administrations in Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Kakinada and Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema have announced holidays for educational institutions on different dates to protect students amid warnings of heavy rainfall and strong winds.
 The closures are not applicable across the entire state. Holiday dates and the types of institutions covered vary by district, so students and parents should check the latest instructions issued by their respective district administrations before travelling to school or college. Reports published on October 26 confirmed precautionary closures in the four districts.
 Andhra Pradesh school holidays on October 27 and 28
 In Visakhapatnam, authorities have declared a two-day holiday on October 27 and 28 for schools across the district. The reported order covers government and private institutions, with the district education authorities warning against violations of the closure directive.
 Anakapalli district has announced a longer closure. Schools will remain shut from October 27 to 29, giving students three consecutive days off as officials prepare for the expected impact of the cyclone. The decision covers government and private schools in the district.
 Kakinada and Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema districts have also announced precautionary holidays for educational institutions on October 27 and 28. The orders were issued in view of the weather threat and the possibility of disruption as the cyclone moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.

 Cyclone Arnab: IMD warns of heavy rain and strong winds
 The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned that Cyclone Arnab is likely to intensify over the west-central Bay of Bengal before moving towards the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts. In its October 26 bulletin, the weather agency said the system was expected to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm on October 27.
 The IMD forecast that the system could cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, by the forenoon of October 28. Maximum sustained wind speeds could reach 115 to 125 kmph, with gusts up to 140 kmph. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also expected in parts of Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam.
 The weather warning has prompted local administrations to take precautionary steps, including suspending classes in vulnerable districts. Students, parents and educational institutions should follow official weather advisories and local administration announcements as conditions develop.
 Are schools closed across Andhra Pradesh?
 No state-wide school holiday has been announced in the reports available as of October 26. The confirmed closures apply to specific districts, and institutions elsewhere in Andhra Pradesh should not assume they will remain shut unless the relevant authorities issue an order.
 Parents and students should check their district administration’s official announcements and contact their schools or colleges for clarification. Further closures may be announced depending on the cyclone’s movement and the severity of rainfall and winds. Residents in coastal and low-lying areas should follow safety instructions issued by local authorities and the IMD.
